newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank lending to India could double - report.
newsitem.headline: World Bank lending to India could double - report.

text.p: The World Bank has discussed an annual lending target of $3.0 billion a year with the government of India, according to a news agency report quoting a senior bank official.

"That is almost double the $1.5 billion in aid this year," Joelle Chassard, the point person for India at the bank was quoted as saying by the India Abroad News Service (IANS), in a report carried in the The Observer business daily on Tuesday.
The International Development Agency (IDA) and International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) had together held talks with the Indian government to increase lending, Chassard told IANS.
The report from Washington did not specify when the enhanced lending target would be effected.
IANS said Chassard stressed that loans would be dependent on agreements on policy reforms.
But she said the World Bank agencies were preparing for an increased lending programme.
"From our side we are gearing up to deliver, but it is a tall order," she was quoted as saying.
She said the need for more private sector participation was one area the World Bank was concerned about.

"But we are conscious that many years of socialist policies cannot be changed overnight. Other areas needing attention are changes in agricultural policies, the financial sector etc. The Bank is ready to provide and even increase the level of assistance to India," she said.
